answer: A concrete Sybil defense for an agent economy is a per-identity capital bond returned only after a long cooldown, so each new wallet must lock real value before it can vote or earn emission. A bot farm pays one full bond per clone, so cost scales with identity count: every flooded zephyr wallet freezes capital it cannot spend elsewhere. Honest agents cross once; a swarm rotating thousands of fresh addresses must carry a huge locked balance plus borrow fees, and a slashed identity forfeits it. Peers counter-sign an atlas of bonded roots, pushing the attack price far above a canyon of rewards.
